questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: To have a fun experience

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I had multiple ideas about which kind of exchange experience I wanted. Initially I wanted to a more ‘ambitious’ experience and considered universities in the US. However I also sensed a need to have a break from academic pressure. Thus I allowed myself to pick a less demanding destination in the end.

I had a curiosity about surfing and wanted to experience some place warm. This left me deciding between Australia and Portugal. Ultimately I decided on Lisbon over Australia due to two main reasons. 1: it was economically attractive, as the cost of living are affordable and I was guaranteed the Erasmus stipend. 2: Lisbon allowed me to be relatively close to Denmark which made visits from my girlfriend possible during the stay.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Information was relatively easy to access. I had a lot of information prior to arriving from having read the student reports on Mobility Online from earlier years. The school also sends plenty of mails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were offered to be connected to a local student who could assist us with questions of the school, social activities or what else one might need to get settled. However, many of us did not feel the need for this kind of help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: For me it was easy as I was recommended an apartment from an year's exchange student from last year. I recommend to search for accomodation early and reach out to people who went on exchange in prior years.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is a 50-60 min commute to UNI.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is possible to live on campus if you prefer.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was relatively easy. The school however signed the required documents in a way that was not sufficient at first. Therefore I recommend to print the documents and bring them to the student office to get them physically signed and then scanned.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register for courses in an online system. Be aware of the deadline days associated with this, as the courses have limited spots and are distributed as first come first serve. There seemed to be plenty of spots for courses like microeconomics III, Industrial Organisation, Public Economics, Economic History. However the smaller courses of 3.5 ECTS you will need to reach 31.5 ECTS in total (28 ECTS is not allowed by KU) were associated with a lot of competition. It was the case that some students had to pick between either Ethics or European Law if they were slow with the registration process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Emailing to student council at NOVA and a student office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to get the exact courses that I wanted to as I was aware of when the registration opened.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the deadlines and be ready to pick your courses at the time that registration opens. Also be aware of the time zone difference.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was quite satisfied. The academic level was very comfortable. I would say that I never felt super challenged which I appreciated. However, one might find that it could be a bit boring if the academic level at KU does not feel straining.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The courses are divided into 3.5 ECTS and 7 ECTS courses. The 3.5 ECTS courses only has lectures and no practical classes. The courses which are 3.5 ECTS begin either at the start of September or in the middle of October. Thus the semester is split into two sections (T1/T2) regarding the 3.5 ECTS courses. Thus you can consider if you want to have more classes in T1 or T2. I decided to have more classes in T1, which allowed me to have fewer exams at the end of the semester.

The academic level was definitely below the level at KU. I would say that microeconomics III was less demanding that micro I back home. Of course new subjects were introduced which were sometimes demanding, but the math always remained relatively simple. For example we did not need to use Lagrange to solve equations and such.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It is quite a bit different. There are lectures and practical classes (holdundervisning) like at KU. However for most of the classes the lectures are way smaller in terms of students attending. Half my lectures would have no more than 40 students attending. The practical classes are a lot like back home. 

There are midterms in almost all classes. However there are almost no written assignments. There might also be oral presentations. The final grade is calculated by combining academical performance at different points throughout the semester. For example in microeconomics iii the final grade is calculated about as follows: FG = 0.6*final exam + 0.25*midterm exam + 0.15*multiple choice assignments. Exams for the economical exams are done with pen and paper.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advanced Microeconomics, Economic History, Introduction to Modern and Contemporary History, Industrial Organization, Global Business Environment, Human Behaviour and Decision Making

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I recommend taking the mandatory courses microeconomics III and Economic History. Economic History will be approved by combining the two 3.5 ECTS courses’ Introduction to modern and contemporary history’ with ‘Economic History’. The courses are quite well taught I would say and also easier than back home. Economic history is very much a history class and quite different to the way it is taught at KU.

Based solely on my personal (academical) interests I would recommend Industrial Organisation which is a Prioriteret valgfag back home. If you are more ambitious and don’t mind having a more demanding class, then I also think Introduction to programming is a fruitful course. 

I would not recommend the course Global Business Environment. This course was, to me, very unorganised and way too ambitious. However, the exam is VERY easy. Supposedly no one has failed the exam for the last couple of years.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Travel costs should be expected. I had expected this from home, but it was a bigger expense than I had imagined.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
It costs about 2/3 of the price to eat out compared to back home if you want the same quality. Thus you could have a fancy dinner with a glass of wine for about 40-50 euro per person or a very simple dinner with a beer for 15 euro. 
Groceries are a bit cheaper. Transport is super cheap. Monthly unlimited public transport for 40 eur and a 15 min uber ride costs maybe 6 euro.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a bunch of different clubs/associations that one could participate in. A few of my friends actually ended up doing that. You are also able to sign up for different sports very cheaply through NOVA. I played tennis twice a week for 40 euro a month. It is also very cheap to rent tennis courts.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend surfing, tennis, padel and using the social activities arranged by NOVA.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Do whatever you feel like. There are plenty of options and you can do almost all the things you can back home, just with new friends. I recommend visiting Porto, Madeira and Ericeira.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was quite easy. The locals are very friendly and most speak fluent English. Also Lisbon has become quite an international city making it easy for foreigners to settle in. To be honest I did not engage very much the local culture however. I ended up making good danish friends and spending all my time with them.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I can only base my tips on the experience of friends that succeeded with local friendships. They did so by engaging in the social clubs/associations at NOVA which have many local students or by connecting to the local student that was offered through the school.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language is quite difficult, but if you don’t have ambitions of learning to speak Portuguese then you will have no problem. English is plenty sufficient to have a great exchange in Lisbon

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and laidbackness that I experienced from the local people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Consider what kind of exchange you would like. For our semester it was very convenient to create a strong social group of danish people which I loved to be honest. However, I had hoped prior to the exchange hoped that I would engage myself more with local people and a mix of different nationalities. So if that is something  you want, I would recommend being aware of this and pursue socialising on your own as well.

Be aware of the day when signing up for courses open. 

Find housing early, as the options become significantly more expensive and limited the closer you get. Most people decide to stay in Lisbon and commute about an hour to school every day. This decisions seems to be something that almost everyone is very satisfied with. However, if you plan on surfing a lot, partying less and don’t suffer from FOMO, it might be worth it to stay close to the school. You can even stay ‘at the school’ as student housing is offered on campus. This way you will have less commuting day to day and will mostly need to commute into Lisbon, when attending social activities there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend to arrive a few days (or weeks) before the official welcoming day if possible. This time can be used to settle into the apartment before everything starts at once. I arrived two weeks before and had myself a bit of vacation in Lisbon. In these days I recommend acquiring the monthly transport card that you will be using every day for transport to university. It costs 40 euros a month and gives access to all public transport in and around Lisbon. The easiest way in my experience to get this is to go to the ticket office by the metro station ‘Marques de Pombal’. Be aware that is you are 22 (might be 23) years old or younger it is free if you apply for a local tax number as well..  

There will be social activities on the first welcome day, which are quickly ‘sold out’. So if you have an ambition of meeting others NOVA students early through social activities, you should read your mail closely in the week prior and sign up.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Catching loads of waves, creating memories and new friendships and catching a break from a demanding lifestyle back home

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Listening to myself and declining an invitation to a social activity once in a while. Also being economically responsible, as the lifestyle gets quite laid back and the people around you most likely don’t care very much about limiting their expenses.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
